summary: The Abay Kunanbayev Scholarship is a merit-based award from Nazarbayev University in Astana for top international applicants. It is given to candidates whom the admissions committee of a school recommends for admission, with no separate scholarship form. The university states that it covers the tuition fee, basic medical insurance and a monthly stipend. The pages tie it to master's and PhD admission.
eligibility_notes:
There is no separate scholarship application. You apply to a programme through the university's online admissions system, go through its selection steps, and are considered by default. The award goes to those whom the admissions committee of the programme's school recommends for admission.

The university says the award is for top international candidates. No countries, minimum grades or number of awards are published. Entry requirements are the same for all candidates whatever their citizenship, and depend on the programme.

Master's admission: a bachelor's degree or equivalent with a CGPA of at least 2.5 out of 4.0 (final-year students may send the current transcript). English: Academic IELTS overall 6.0 (writing 6.0, other parts 5.5) or equivalent TOEFL; some programmes differ (MBA writing 5.5; Doctor of Medicine IELTS 6.5 with no part below 6.0). Exemption is at the committee's discretion for people with a degree from an English-speaking country or an English-taught degree, or NU graduates. Many programmes add work experience, a statement of purpose and recommendation letters.

PhD admission: a CGPA of at least 2.75 out of 4.0 in the master's (or bachelor's and/or master's depending on the school). English: IELTS overall 6.5 with no part below 6.0, or equivalent TOEFL; Eurasian Studies needs IELTS 7.0 with no part below 6.0. IELTS Online, IELTS Indicator, TOEFL iBT Home Edition and TOEFL PDT are not accepted.

A person who already earned a master's or PhD in Kazakhstan on a state scholarship cannot receive the same degree on a state grant again (this rule is in the FAQ and is not specific to the Abay award).
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated. Work experience depends on the programme: for example the MBA asks for about 3 years, the Executive MBA 5 years, Master in Public Policy 2 years, Master in Public Administration 3 years and Educational Leadership/Multilingual Education 1 year; the committee may consider less. Most other master's and PhD programmes state none.
funding_summary: The university says the scholarship covers the tuition fee, basic medical insurance and a monthly stipend. For comparison, tuition per year without a scholarship is USD 16,000 for master's and USD 23,500 for doctoral study (2025/2026). The stipend is the same for all students whatever their citizenship. The pages do not say for how many years the scholarship is held or what is needed to keep it.
programmes_note: The pages read do not restrict the scholarship to particular fields. The university's programme list for master's and doctoral study is on its Programs A-Z page: 32 master's programmes and 22 doctoral programmes were listed there. All master's and PhD programmes are taught in English, except the Executive MBA, which is in English with simultaneous interpretation into Russian. Graduate programmes are listed under the schools of Medicine, Engineering, Computing and AI, Sciences and Humanities, Business, Public Policy and Education.
institutions_note: Nazarbayev University only (Astana). The scholarship is recommended by the admissions committee of each of its schools.

summary.detail: Merit-based scholarship for top international applicants recommended for admission. Taught in English (the Executive MBA with simultaneous interpretation into Russian). Entry: bachelor's degree with CGPA at least 2.5 out of 4.0 and English proof; programme length and number of awards not stated. Stipend for master's students per the FAQ: 200,000 tenge a month (another FAQ lists 218,750 tenge, so confirm with the university).

benefits.conditions: Without a scholarship tuition is USD 16,000 per year for master's and USD 23,500 per year for doctoral study (2025/2026 figures).

benefits.limit_text: Monthly stipend, the same for all students whatever their citizenship: master's 200,000 tenge, PhD 240,000 tenge (FAQ figures)
benefits.conditions: Another FAQ on the same site gives 218,750 tenge for master's and 262,500 tenge for PhD; the pages do not explain the difference. Confirm the current amount with the university.

benefits.limit_text: The pages say accommodation is guaranteed for international students; a dormitory is estimated at about USD 55 a month
benefits.conditions: The scholarship description does not list accommodation as covered.

benefits.limit_text: Travel is not listed as covered

requirements.text: Academic transcripts (final-year students may send the current transcript, with full documents required later).

Letters of recommendation. Referees receive an automatic e-mail request after you submit the form. The number depends on the programme (usually two; PhD letters from the last 12 months or two years depending on school).

Proof of English proficiency: IELTS or TOEFL (valid at submission, two years; sent by the test centre to the university and also uploaded as a scan with its certificate number). Master's: IELTS 6.0 overall, writing 6.0, other parts 5.5. PhD: IELTS 6.5 overall, no part below 6.0 (Eurasian Studies 7.0).
requirements.conditional_rule: Not needed for applicants who studied in English or hold a degree from an English-speaking country, at the committee's discretion

requirements.text: Copy of passport (national ID for citizens of Kazakhstan).

Statement of purpose or personal statement, for programmes that require it (for example Political Science and International Relations, Eurasian Studies, Medicine, Engineering Management, all PhD schools).
Research proposal, writing sample or project proposal.
requirements.conditional_rule: Some PhD programmes (for example Eurasian Studies, Business, Public Policy, Education, Medicine)
Required for MBA, MSc Finance, Business PhD and Engineering Management unless waived; optional or recommended elsewhere

requirements.text: One 3x4 photo uploaded to the online profile.

requirements.conditional_rule: School of Medicine PhD applicants only (equivalent form for international applicants)

requirements.text: Non-refundable application fee of 15,000 tenge paid online (tripled in the last two weeks before the first approved deadline and during an extension); a refundable guarantee fee of 100,000 tenge is paid by graduate admits.

application_steps.title: Create an account and choose your programme
application_steps.detail: Register on the university admissions portal, choose Master's or PhD, and confirm your e-mail. You may apply to at most two master's or PhD programmes and must choose one if admitted to both. There is no separate scholarship application: all candidates are considered by default.

application_steps.title: Complete the form and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Fill in the application form with the data consent, upload the documents and a 3x4 photo, then pay the 15,000 tenge application fee online and submit. Changes are not possible after submission. Recommendation letters are requested from your referees automatically by e-mail.

application_steps.title: Send English test results and any GRE or GMAT
application_steps.detail: Have the test centre send IELTS or TOEFL results electronically to the university (allow at least 7 to 10 working days), and upload a scan with the certificate number. Results arriving after the deadline are not considered. Deadlines for 2027-2028 were shown as to be announced.

application_steps.title: Committee review and shortlisting
application_steps.detail: The admissions committee of each school reviews the full package (motivation, transcripts, recommendations) and shortlists eligible candidates for interview. Each committee has its own evaluation method; it looks at academic skills, competitiveness, motivation and likely contribution to the university.

application_steps.title: Interview in English
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by the admissions committee by video call or face to face. PhD interviews last at least 15 minutes and are held in English. The committee recommends scholarship holders from the candidates it admits.

application_steps.title: Notification of results
application_steps.detail: Selected candidates are told by e-mail and can find the offer letter in their personal account.

application_steps.title: Accept the offer and complete enrolment steps
application_steps.detail: Admission requires completing orientation week and signing a contract with the school. Graduate admits pay a refundable guarantee fee of 100,000 tenge, returned in the second semester after signing the education services agreement, attending orientation and finishing the first semester in good standing. International students need authorisation to study (a study visa); the visa steps were not readable on the pages read.

fetch_problems: Several nu.edu.kz pages were returned truncated by the page reader (master's regular admissions, master's financial aid page), so the Tuition fees section of the master's page and the master's financial aid page text could not be read in full.
The Visa and Documents page is only an overview; the Study Visa Requirements and Accommodation sub-pages were not opened.
notes: Stipend figures in the university FAQ conflict (master's 200,000 vs 218,750 tenge; PhD 240,000 vs 262,500 tenge). The file gives the first set and flags the second.

The master's regular admissions page gives IELTS 6.0; a web search snippet suggested the university's separate master's admission policy document says 6.5. That document was not opened, so check the programme page.

NU also offers citizenship-based partial scholarships covering 50% to 90% of tuition, and 200 PhD scholarships for its 15th anniversary; these are separate from the Abay scholarship and not described here beyond this note.
Stored teaching language 'English' is confirmed by the FAQ.
Master's level confirmation is carried over from stored data (the master's page text read was truncated); the PhD page and the FAQ were read directly.
